description: Count distinct executed orders per order type, so each order counts once however many fills it has, and then compute shares and the above-average summary from those counts.

b.request: Count distinct orders with at least one matching execution for each `ordertune`, grouping missing types together; compute each type’s share of all such distinct orders, then return the sum of counts, average share, and average excess over the overall average share for types whose share is strictly above that average
b.sql:
WITH type_counts AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(o.ordertune, 'Missing') AS ordertune, COUNT(DISTINCT o.recordvault) AS order_count
  FROM orders o
  JOIN orderexecutions e ON e.ordersmark = o.recordvault
  GROUP BY COALESCE(o.ordertune, 'Missing')
), type_shares AS (
  SELECT ordertune, order_count, order_count::numeric / SUM(order_count) OVER () AS share
  FROM type_counts
), overall AS (
  SELECT SUM(order_count) AS total_orders, AVG(share) AS average_share
  FROM type_shares
)
SELECT SUM(ts.order_count) AS sum_counts,
       AVG(ts.share) AS average_share,
       AVG(ts.share - ov.average_share) FILTER (WHERE ts.share > ov.average_share) AS average_excess
FROM type_shares ts
CROSS JOIN overall ov;

a.request: Link each order execution to its order (where `recordvault` matches `ordersmark`), and drop any execution without a matching order. Count distinct orders per order type (`ordertune`); an order with several executions counts only once, and a missing order type forms its own group. Then work out each type's share of the total count as a fraction. Looking only at the order types whose share is strictly above the average share across all order types, return a single unrounded row with: the sum of their counts, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds that overall average share.
a.sql:
WITH type_counts AS (
  SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(DISTINCT o.recordvault) AS order_count
  FROM orderexecutions oe
  JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = oe.ordersmark
  GROUP BY o.ordertune
), shares AS (
  SELECT order_count, order_count::numeric / SUM(order_count) OVER () AS share
  FROM type_counts
), overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(share) AS average_share FROM shares
)
SELECT SUM(s.order_count) AS sum_counts,
       AVG(s.share) AS average_share,
       AVG(s.share - x.average_share) AS average_excess_share
FROM shares s
CROSS JOIN overall x
WHERE s.share > x.average_share

c.request: Link each order execution to its order (where `recordvault` matches `ordersmark`), and ignore executions without a matching order. Find how many executed orders each order type (`ordertune`) has, with a missing order type treated as its own group. Then work out each type's share of the total as a fraction. Looking only at the order types whose share is strictly above the average share across all order types, return a single unrounded row with: the sum of their counts, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds that overall average share. Count distinct executed orders per order type, so each order counts once however many fills it has, and then compute shares and the above-average summary from those counts.
c.sql:
WITH executed_orders AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT o.orderspivot, o.ordertune
  FROM orders AS o
  INNER JOIN orderexecutions AS oe
    ON oe.ordersmark = o.recordvault
), type_counts AS (
  SELECT ordertune, COUNT(*) AS order_count
  FROM executed_orders
  GROUP BY ordertune
), shares AS (
  SELECT ordertune,
         order_count,
         order_count::numeric / SUM(order_count) OVER () AS share
  FROM type_counts
), overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(share) AS average_share
  FROM shares
)
SELECT SUM(s.order_count) AS sum_counts,
       AVG(s.share) AS average_share,
       AVG(s.share - o.average_share) AS average_excess_share
FROM shares AS s
CROSS JOIN overall AS o
WHERE s.share > o.average_share

d.request: Link each order execution to its order where `recordvault` matches `ordersmark`, ignoring executions without a matching order. For each order type (`ordertune`), count distinct executed orders so each order is counted once regardless of how many fills it has; treat a missing order type as its own group. Calculate each type’s share of the total count. Among types whose share is strictly above the average share across all order types, return one unrounded row containing the sum of their counts, their average share, and the average amount by which their shares exceed the overall average share.
d.sql:
WITH type_counts AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(o.ordertune, '<missing>') AS order_type,
         COUNT(DISTINCT o.recordvault) AS order_count
  FROM orderexecutions AS e
  JOIN orders AS o ON o.recordvault = e.ordersmark
  GROUP BY COALESCE(o.ordertune, '<missing>')
),
shares AS (
  SELECT order_type,
         order_count,
         order_count::numeric / SUM(order_count) OVER () AS share
  FROM type_counts
),
scored AS (
  SELECT *, AVG(share) OVER () AS overall_avg_share
  FROM shares
)
SELECT SUM(order_count) AS total_order_count,
       AVG(share) AS average_share,
       AVG(share - overall_avg_share) AS average_excess_share
FROM scored
WHERE share > overall_avg_share;
